title: Error Handling and Debugging
description: Learn how to identify, handle, and debug errors in JavaScript to create more reliable and maintainable code.

lessons.title: Introduction to Errors
lessons.content: Errors are unexpected problems that occur during code execution. Understanding error types helps you write code that anticipates and handles failures gracefully.

lessons.title: Common JavaScript Errors
lessons.content: Typical JavaScript errors include SyntaxError, ReferenceError, TypeError, and RangeError. Each error type gives clues about the problem source.

lessons.title: Using try-catch
lessons.content: The `try-catch` block lets you run code that may fail and handle errors without stopping the whole program.

lessons.title: Example: try-catch
Throwing Custom Errors
lessons.content: You can create and throw your own errors using `throw` to signal unexpected situations in your code.

lessons.title: Example: throw Error
Using finally Block
lessons.content: The `finally` block runs code after try and catch, regardless of whether an error was thrown, useful for cleanup tasks.

lessons.title: Example: try-catch-finally
Debugging with Console
lessons.content: Using `console.log`, `console.error`, and other console methods helps track variables and understand code flow during development.

lessons.title: Browser DevTools and Debugger
lessons.content: Modern browsers provide developer tools with debugging features like breakpoints, step execution, and inspecting variables to help find and fix issues.
